findings.evidence: The proof already shows `∀ θ, deriv (circleMap z₀ r) θ / (circleMap z₀ r θ - z₀) = Complex.I` at lines 56-61 and then uses `intervalIntegral.integral_const` at line 63, whose Mathlib form is `∫ _ in a..b, c = (b - a) • c` (`mathlib/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/IntervalIntegral/Basic.lean:835`). The roadmap’s general `windingNumber` also takes arbitrary endpoints `a b` (`roadmap/TauCetiRoadmap/ContourIntegration/Targets.lean:76`).
findings.fix: Use the natural interval form, e.g. `theorem windingNumber_modelSector {z₀ : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≠ 0) (a b : ℝ) : (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I)⁻¹ * ∫ θ in a..b, deriv (circleMap z₀ r) θ / (circleMap z₀ r θ - z₀) = ((b - a : ℝ) : ℂ) / (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ))`, then recover the current theorem and the `π`/`π/3` specializations by setting `a = 0`.
findings.issue: `windingNumber_modelSector` hard-codes `∫ θ in 0..α`, so it only applies directly to arcs whose parameter interval starts at `0`, although the model-sector calculation is independent of the starting angle.

summary: The main computation is under-generalized: the proof establishes a start-angle-independent integrand but the public theorem only exposes arcs beginning at `0`. State the arbitrary-interval arc theorem first, then derive the roadmap special cases from it.
